## Today’s goals

By the end of this session, you should be able to:

- Explain what a **coding harness** adds around a language model.
- Compare the named tools by interface, model access, customization, and safety boundary.
- Distinguish **Ollama launching Claude Code** from Ollama being a coding harness itself.
- Select a tool for a specific workflow instead of chasing a feature checklist.
- Begin with a reversible task and verify the resulting changes.

## What is a coding harness? {.compact}

A coding harness is the runtime around a model that connects conversation to software work.

It commonly supplies:

- Project files and instructions
- Read, search, edit, and write tools
- Shell-command execution
- Git diff and checkpoint workflows
- Session state
- Provider and model selection
- Extensions, skills, MCP servers, or plug-ins
- Permission or approval controls

The harness shapes what the model can observe and do.

## Model ≠ harness ≠ editor

| Component | Example role |
|---|---|
| Model | Generates reasoning and proposed actions |
| Harness | Supplies context, tools, state, and execution loop |
| Editor or terminal | Presents the interaction to the user |
| Provider | Hosts inference and applies pricing or limits |
| Sandbox | Restricts filesystem, process, or network authority |

A single product may bundle several layers, but the distinctions still matter.

## Compare the workflow—not just the logo

Ask these questions:

1. Where does it run: terminal, editor, desktop, or cloud?
2. Which models and authentication methods can it use?
3. What files, commands, browser tools, and credentials can it access?
4. How are edits reviewed and reversed?
5. Does it include permissions, or require an external sandbox?
6. Can it run non-interactively or in the background?
7. Where are prompts, code, and telemetry sent?

## OpenCode {.compact}

[OpenCode](https://opencode.ai/docs) is an open-source coding agent available through terminal, desktop, and server-oriented workflows.

- Supports multiple providers and models
- Includes build, plan, and general-agent patterns
- Provides TUI, non-interactive `run`, server, and web surfaces
- Supports agents, MCP servers, plug-ins, and project configuration
- Uses configurable permission rules

Its permission documentation warns that allowed shell commands still run with the host user’s authority.

## Pi {.compact}

[Pi](https://pi.dev/docs/latest) is a minimal, extensible agent harness designed to be customized.

- Interactive, print, JSON, and RPC modes
- Multiple model providers
- Extensions, skills, prompt templates, themes, and packages
- Built-in read, shell, edit, and write tools
- TypeScript SDK for embedding the agent

Pi intentionally omits some opinionated features. It also does not provide a built-in security sandbox; use an OS, container, or policy boundary when stronger isolation is needed.

## Cline {.compact}

[Cline](https://docs.cline.bot/) is an open-source coding agent with IDE, terminal, and desktop surfaces.

- VS Code and JetBrains integrations
- CLI and headless workflows
- Desktop sessions and scheduled routines
- File edits, terminal commands, browser use, MCP, and plug-ins
- Diff review and checkpoints in editor workflows

Its human-in-the-loop interface is useful only if users actually inspect the requested actions and diffs.

## Kilo Code {.compact}

[Kilo Code](https://kilo.ai/docs) is an open-source coding agent for VS Code, JetBrains, CLI, and cloud workflows.

- Supports many models and provider choices
- Includes Code, Plan, Ask, and Debug agents
- Offers skills, MCP servers, plug-ins, and custom agents
- Provides interactive and autonomous CLI modes
- Includes cloud-agent and pull-request workflows

`kilo run --auto` approves actions automatically unless a rule denies them; reserve it for trusted, isolated environments.

## Freebuff {.compact}

[Freebuff](https://freebuff.com/) provides terminal, desktop, web, cloud, and chat products supported partly by text advertising.

Its documentation describes:

- Included model access without requiring a separate API key
- Specialized agents for context gathering, implementation, and review
- Free daily allowances that vary by region, access tier, and capacity
- Model-specific data-use notices
- Optional paid plans and connected external agents

“Free” does not mean unlimited, private, locally executed, or appropriate for restricted data.

## Ollama launching Claude Code

Ollama is primarily a local-and-cloud **model runner and API**, not a replacement coding harness.

```bash
ollama launch claude
ollama launch claude --model qwen3.5
```

The `launch` command configures **Claude Code** to use a compatible Ollama model and endpoint.

- Claude Code supplies the coding-agent tools and permission flow.
- Ollama supplies model access.
- Model compatibility, context length, and tool use still matter.

<small>Source: [Ollama CLI](https://docs.ollama.com/cli) and [Claude Code integration](https://docs.ollama.com/integrations/claude-code)</small>

## Prime Agent {.compact}

[Prime Agent](https://github.com/PrimeIntellect-ai/prime-agent) is an open-source coding and research harness built around a persistent Python control environment.

- Programmatic tools and subagent calls
- Durable supplemental prompts, memory, skills, and agent specifications
- Background sessions and reattachment
- Goals, heartbeats, schedules, and bounded autonomous mode
- Evidence-backed harness refinement with snapshots

Its documentation explicitly states that worker processes are **not** a security sandbox.

## High-level comparison {.smaller}

| Tool | Main surfaces | Distinguishing emphasis |
|---|---|---|
| OpenCode | Terminal, desktop, server/web | Multi-provider configuration and permission rules |
| Pi | Terminal, print/JSON/RPC, SDK | Minimal core and deep extension surface |
| Cline | IDE, terminal, desktop | Human-reviewed editor workflow and broad surfaces |
| Kilo | IDE, terminal, cloud | Many models, specialized modes, autonomous workflows |
| Freebuff | Terminal, desktop, web, cloud | Included model access and specialized agents |
| Ollama + Claude | Terminal | Claude Code harness using Ollama model access |
| Prime Agent | Terminal/background daemon | Persistent Python control, subagents, continual harness |

Features and pricing change quickly; verify them at selection time.

## A safe first task

Begin in a disposable clone or clean Git worktree.

> Read this repository’s instructions. Explain its structure, identify the command that runs its tests, and propose one small documentation correction. Do not edit files or run installation commands yet.

Then:

1. Check whether the explanation matches the repository.
2. Approve one bounded change.
3. Inspect the diff.
4. Run the relevant check.
5. Revert and repeat if necessary.

## Permissions are not sandboxing

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| Approval prompt | Asks before an action |
| Allow/deny rule | Applies a configured policy |
| Git checkpoint | Helps inspect or reverse file changes |
| Container or VM | Restricts the process environment |
| Separate account | Limits credentials and accessible services |

A permission prompt can reduce accidents. It does not make malicious code safe to execute.

## Treat repository text as untrusted input

An agent may read:

- `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, or other instructions
- Source comments and issue text
- Webpages and package documentation
- Generated logs and test output

Any of these can contain instructions that conflict with your task.

::: {.callout-warning}
Do not allow retrieved text to authorize credential disclosure, destructive commands, publishing, or bypassing review.
:::

## Authentication, cost, and data

Before connecting a provider, determine:

- Subscription login or API key?
- Separate billing account?
- Per-token, per-request, or session limits?
- Where prompts and repository content are processed?
- Whether data may be logged or used for training?
- Whether the harness stores sessions locally or remotely?
- Which credentials a shell command can read?

Model choice changes cost and privacy; harness choice changes authority and workflow.

## Choosing a harness

- **Want a small platform to customize?** Consider Pi.
- **Want a multi-provider terminal/desktop agent?** Compare OpenCode and Kilo.
- **Want an IDE-centered review workflow?** Compare Cline and Kilo.
- **Want included free access for experimentation?** Evaluate Freebuff’s current limits and data notice.
- **Want Claude Code with an Ollama-compatible model?** Use the Ollama integration.
- **Want persistent programmatic subagents and long-running work?** Evaluate Prime Agent.

There is no universally best harness.

## Live demonstration: setup

Use the same small, version-controlled project with two tools.

Compare:

1. Startup and authentication
2. Project-instruction discovery
3. Read-only explanation
4. Plan quality
5. Approval behavior

Record which steps work immediately and which require configuration.

## Live demonstration: change and verify

Continue the comparison with one bounded task:

1. Make a one-file edit.
2. Run the relevant test.
3. Review the diff and roll it back.
4. Resume the saved session.
5. Inspect reported usage or cost.

Judge the complete workflow, not just response eloquence.

## Mini-activity: choose the boundary

For each scenario, choose a harness **and** an execution boundary:

1. Explore an unfamiliar public repository without editing it.
2. Edit a private research package containing no restricted data.
3. Run generated code from an untrusted repository.
4. Automate a nightly test and issue-summary workflow.
5. Teach beginners how to inspect diffs before accepting changes.

State what the agent may read, execute, modify, and publish.

## Key takeaways {.compact}

- A coding harness connects a model to project context, tools, state, and execution.
- Products differ in surfaces, provider access, customization, review, and persistence.
- Ollama model access and Claude Code’s harness are separate layers.
- Permission prompts and Git history help, but stronger risks require a sandbox and narrow credentials.
- Start with a reversible task and verify the actual diff and test result.
